title: The Lantern at Dusk
description: A terrible blight is spreading from the old barrow in the hills — the same barrow where a cursed lantern was buried centuries ago. The lantern must be brought to a stone circle in the valley to break the curse. But the barrow is not empty.
author: Nicholas A. Gasper
notes: A one-shot introductory adventure showcasing core mechanics.

bestiary.name: Duskwight
bestiary.description: A restless spirit bound to the barrow. It drifts through the corridors, its form flickering like a dying candle. It does not attack unless provoked, but it will not let anyone pass without an offering.

sb_spends.name: Draining Touch
sb_spends.effect: A PC is touched by cold dread; they mark 1 Fatigue.

sb_spends.name: Terrifying Visage
sb_spends.effect: The Duskwight reveals its true form; a PC must test Spirit+Resolve (DV 3) or be Frightened (-1 die to all actions for one exchange).

sb_spends.name: Fade to Mist
sb_spends.effect: The Duskwight becomes incorporeal for one exchange, avoiding all physical attacks.

bestiary.lore: They were once guardians of the lantern, sworn to protect it from those who would misuse its power. They do not remember their names, only their duty.

bestiary.name: Quick Lena
bestiary.description: A brash young treasure hunter with quick fingers and a quicker temper. She's here for the lantern, and she doesn't intend to share.

sb_spends.name: Dirty Trick
sb_spends.effect: Lena throws dust in a PC's eyes; they act at Desperate for one exchange.

sb_spends.name: Slippery Escape
sb_spends.effect: Lena disengages from melee and moves to Near range without provoking opportunity.

sb_spends.name: Taunt
sb_spends.effect: Lena insults a PC, goading them into a reckless action; their next attack is at -1 die.

bestiary.lore: She's been chasing legends since she was a child. She doesn't know what the lantern does—she just knows it's worth something to someone.

bestiary.name: Barrow Guardian
bestiary.description: A crude statue of a warrior, animated by ancient magic. It stands motionless until the lantern is disturbed, then it lurches into action, its stone limbs grinding.

sb_spends.name: Stone Fist
sb_spends.effect: A PC is knocked Prone; they must spend an action to stand.

sb_spends.name: Shatter the Ground
sb_spends.effect: The Guardian slams the floor; all in Near must test Body+Athletics (DV 3) or be Slowed for one exchange.

sb_spends.name: Rumbling Charge
sb_spends.effect: The Guardian charges in a straight line; any PC in its path must test Body+Athletics (DV 4) or take Harm 2.

bestiary.lore: It was built to protect the lantern, but it has stood so long that it has forgotten its purpose. It attacks anything that moves, hoping to remember why it exists.

acts.title: The Lantern at Dusk
acts.description: Enter the barrow, face the Duskwights, confront Quick Lena, escape the collapse, and break the curse.

scenes.title: Scene 1 — The Entry
scenes.description: The barrow entrance is a narrow stone passage. A faint green glow pulses from deeper inside. A cave-in blocks the way.

timers.name: Barrow Collapse
timers.description: Ticks on failure inside. At 6, the entrance seals.

outcomes.clean: You clear the rubble and enter.
outcomes.partial: You get through but disturb rubble — tick Barrow Collapse +1.
outcomes.miss: You are pinned by a rock — mark Harm 1 and tick Collapse +1.

scenes.title: Scene 2 — The Spirit Corridor
scenes.description: The passage widens into a hall where three Duskwights drift. They do not attack unless provoked, but they will not let anyone pass without an offering.

encounters.name: Offer a Memory or a Secret

outcomes.clean: They bow and let you pass.
outcomes.partial: They take your offering but also steal a random piece of equipment.
outcomes.miss: They attack as a single mob (Cap 2, Harm 1 each, 2 Fatigue each on hit).

outcomes.clean: You defeat the Duskwights and pass through.
outcomes.partial: You drive them back, but they remain in the shadows — they will return later.
outcomes.miss: They overwhelm you; each PC takes Harm 2 and the Barrow Collapse timer advances by 2.

scenes.title: Scene 3 — The Lantern Chamber
scenes.description: The lantern sits on a stone altar. Quick Lena is there, trying to pry it loose.

timers.name: Lena's Agenda
timers.description: Ticks each scene inside. At 4, Lena takes the lantern first.

outcomes.clean: She leaves peacefully, but warns that 'others will come for it.'
outcomes.partial: She agrees to split any reward but demands a favor later (start a Debt Timer [4]).
outcomes.miss: She triggers a trap — a stone door starts closing (tick Collapse +2).

scenes.title: Scene 4 — Escape
scenes.description: After you take the lantern, the barrow begins to collapse in earnest. The party needs 3 successes before 2 failures to escape.

timers.name: Barrow Collapse
timers.description: Ticks on failure. At 6, entrance seals.

outcomes.clean: Each success counts toward the 3 needed; no extra tick.
outcomes.miss: Tick Collapse +1. If Collapse reaches 6, entrance seals — find another way.

scenes.title: Resolution — Breaking the Curse
scenes.description: Return the lantern to the stone circle. Breaking the curse requires a simple ritual.

outcomes.clean: The blight lifts. Elder Sarai rewards each PC with a String — 'The village owes you.'
outcomes.partial: The curse lifts, but the lantern cannot be destroyed — it will attract another danger soon.
outcomes.miss: The curse is only pushed back one year. A dark spirit escapes and will become a recurring enemy.

npcs.name: Elder Sarai
npcs.motivation: Save her village from the blight.

locations.name: The Old Barrow
locations.description: A moss-covered stone mound on a hill overlooking Duskwood.

locations.name: The Stone Circle
locations.description: A ring of standing stones in the valley below the barrow.

campaignTimers.name: Barrow Collapse
campaignTimers.description: Ticks when the party fails a roll inside. At 6, the entrance seals.

triggers.message: The entrance seals! Escape becomes a Desperate group action.

campaignTimers.name: Lena's Agenda
campaignTimers.description: Ticks at the end of each scene inside the barrow. When it fills, Lena has already taken the lantern.

_gmhints.tone: THIS ADVENTURE IS A TUTORIAL. The tone should be clear, encouraging, and slightly instructional — like a friendly GM showing new players how the game works. The narration should be vivid but not overwhelming, and every mechanic should be explained as it arises. This is the adventure that comes with the GM guide, so it has a pedagogical purpose: teach Position & DV, Outcomes, Timers, and Story Beats through play. Lean into the teaching moments. When a player fails a roll, explain how that generates Story Beats. When a timer ticks, explain what it means. When a Clean Success happens, describe why it feels good. This is not the adventure to be mysterious or withholding — it's the adventure to say 'Here's how the game works, and here's why it's fun.'

pacing.act1: This is a single-act tutorial adventure designed for 1-2 sessions. Each scene introduces a new core mechanic, building complexity as the party progresses through the barrow. Keep the pace brisk — this is not a slow-burn horror investigation, it's a 'learn by doing' dungeon crawl.
pacing.scene_entry: Scene 1: Introduces the core roll mechanic (Position, DV, Outcomes). Explain to players: 'Controlled Position means you have the upper hand — you're not in immediate danger. DV 3 means you need 3 successes to get a Clean Success. The barrow is dangerous, but you're approaching it carefully.' The Barrow Collapse timer is introduced here — this is the first 'ticking clock' mechanic. Explain it as: 'The barrow is unstable. Every failure inside makes it more likely to collapse. This timer represents that pressure — it's not a punishment, it's dramatic tension.' This scene is about the party's first action as a group. Encourage teamwork: if one character has Body+Athletics, they can lead; others can assist (spend a Boon to give +1 die).
pacing.scene_spirit: Scene 2: Introduces social encounters and alternative resolutions. The Duskwights are not combat-first — they can be bargained with. This teaches players that violence is not always the answer. The 'Offer a Memory or a Secret' encounter demonstrates that DV can be modified by player creativity: a particularly meaningful offering might lower the DV. The combat encounter teaches that sometimes violence is necessary, and that Desperate Position means the odds are against you — but victory is still possible with clever play. This is also the first encounter that uses a creature's SB spends — the Duskwight's 'Draining Touch' and 'Terrifying Visage' demonstrate how enemies can complicate a scene without just dealing damage.
pacing.scene_lantern: Scene 3: Introduces the rival NPC and the second timer (Lena's Agenda). Quick Lena is not a villain — she's a competitor with her own goals. This teaches players that NPCs have motivations and that negotiation is possible. The Clean Outcome (she leaves peacefully) rewards non-violence; the Partial Outcome creates a Debt (a future complication); the Miss triggers a trap and ticks the timer. This scene also teaches that timers can interact — Lena's Agenda ticking means she might take the lantern first, raising the stakes. The Barrow Collapse timer is still ticking, so there's pressure from multiple angles. Use this to teach players about resource management: should they spend Boons to succeed quickly, or save them for the escape?
pacing.scene_escape: Scene 4: Introduces the group challenge — 3 successes before 2 failures. This is a classic 'skill challenge' format. Explain to players: 'This is a Desperate Position escape — the barrow is collapsing around you. Each success brings you closer to safety. Each failure makes the collapse worse. You need to work together.' This is the climax of the mechanical tutorial: everything they've learned (Position, DV, Outcomes, Timers) comes together in a high-stakes group roll. Encourage players to describe their actions creatively — using different skills for different obstacles.
pacing.scene_resolution: Resolution: Introduces the 'Ritual of Breaking' — a low-DV Controlled encounter that demonstrates how Clean, Partial, and Miss outcomes create narrative consequences beyond just success/failure. This is the 'reward' scene — the party has survived, and now they see the results of their choices. Clean Success means the village is saved and the party gains a String (a narrative asset). Partial Success means the lantern survives as a future plot hook. Miss means the curse is merely postponed — a recurring enemy is born. This teaches players that their actions have lasting consequences, and that Fate's Edge is a game about narrative as much as mechanics.

core_mechanics.position: Explain Position as: 'Controlled = you have the advantage. Desperate = the odds are against you. Dominant = you're in control. Position affects the stakes, not just the difficulty — a Clean Success in Desperate feels more heroic.'
core_mechanics.dv: Explain DV as: 'The number of successes you need. More successes = better outcome. DV 3 is a typical challenge; DV 5 is a major obstacle.'
core_mechanics.outcomes: Explain Outcomes as: 'Clean = you succeed without complication. Partial = you succeed, but something goes wrong. Miss = you fail and the situation gets worse. Partial and Miss generate Story Beats — this is how the game rewards failure, by giving you narrative resources.'
core_mechanics.timers: Explain Timers as: 'A countdown that builds tension. When a timer fills, something bad (or interesting) happens. Timers are not punishments — they're dramatic tools that raise the stakes.'
core_mechanics.story_beats: Explain Story Beats as: 'A currency the GM can spend to add complications. When you fail a roll, you generate a Story Beat — the GM can use it to make the scene more interesting. This means failure is never boring.'
core_mechanics.boons: Explain Boons as: 'A currency players can spend to improve their odds. You gain Boons by failing rolls, so even failure is a kind of progress. Spend Boons wisely — they're your resource for turning failure into success.'

scene_specific_teaching.scene_entry: When a player rolls to clear the rubble, explicitly call out: 'You're rolling Body+Athletics against DV 3 in Controlled Position. You need 3 successes for a Clean Success. What do you do?' This models the GM's role in calling for rolls.
scene_specific_teaching.scene_spirit: When a player offers a memory, say: 'That's a great idea. Because you're offering something meaningful, I'll lower the DV to 2. This is how creative roleplay can affect mechanics.'
scene_specific_teaching.scene_lantern: When Lena appears, say: 'This is Quick Lena. She's a rival — not necessarily an enemy. You can negotiate, threaten, or try to outsmart her. Remember: social rolls work just like combat rolls. You're testing Presence+Sway against her Resolve.'
scene_specific_teaching.scene_escape: During the escape, say: 'This is a group challenge. Each player can describe what they're doing to help the party escape. You're all rolling Body+Athletics (or whatever makes sense) against DV 3. Desperate Position, so the stakes are high. We need 3 successes before 2 failures. Good luck.'
scene_specific_teaching.scene_resolution: During the ritual, say: 'This is a low-stakes roll — DV 2 in Controlled Position. You've already done the hard part. Now we see how well you seal the curse. The outcome here will affect what happens after the adventure.'

new_player_tips.first_roll: When the first player rolls, explain the dice: 'You're rolling 2d10 against DV 3. Each die that meets or exceeds the DV is a success. 10s count as two successes — that's a critical. Let's see what happens.'
new_player_tips.failure_explanation: When a player fails a roll, say: 'That's a Miss. You didn't succeed, but you gain a Story Beat. The GM can spend that Story Beat to make things interesting. Failure in Fate's Edge is never just failure — it's a story opportunity.'
new_player_tips.boon_use: When a player is about to fail, remind them: 'You have Boons to spend. You can spend a Boon to reroll a die, or to add a die to your pool. Do you want to use one? This is what they're for.'
new_player_tips.assist_explanation: When a player wants to help another, say: 'You can spend a Boon to assist — that gives your ally +1 die to their roll. Teamwork is powerful in Fate's Edge.'

npcSecrets.elder-sarai: Sarai is sincere — she genuinely wants to save her village. She doesn't know the full history of the lantern, only that it was buried to stop the blight. She will offer the party a String (a social asset) as a reward, but she cannot pay in coin. Her village is poor, but grateful.
npcSecrets.quick-lena: Lena is not evil — she's ambitious and reckless. She doesn't know what the lantern does, only that someone in the city will pay handsomely for 'ancient artifacts.' She is in over her head. If the party is kind to her, she may become a recurring ally (or rival). If they are cruel, she will remember. Her true motivation: she wants to prove she's more than a common thief.
npcSecrets.duskwights: The Duskwights were once guardians of the lantern, sworn to protect it. They do not remember their names, only their duty. They are tragic figures, not monsters. If the party offers a meaningful memory (not just a 'secret' but something real), the Duskwights will bow and let them pass. They are testing the party's worth.

forbiddenEarlyRevelations: That the lantern cannot be destroyed — this is a Partial Outcome reveal in the Resolution scene; do not telegraph it early
That Lena is working for someone else — this is a potential recurring plot hook; let her mention 'someone in the city' vaguely, but do not name the patron
That the Duskwights were once human — this is the emotional weight of the Spirit Corridor; let it emerge through roleplay, not GM exposition
That the Barrow Guardian exists — it appears only if the party disturbs the lantern; do not foreshadow it heavily

tutorialTactics.call_rolls_explicitly: Always call rolls with the [ROLL] tag embedded, and explain why: 'You edge toward the rubble, [ROLL "Character" Body+Athletics DV 3 Controlled] to see if you can clear a path without causing a collapse.' This models the GM's role.
tutorialTactics.explain_outcomes: After each roll, explain what happened in mechanical terms: 'That's a Clean Success — you clear the rubble without any trouble. The barrow is stable for now.' 'That's a Partial — you make it through, but the rubble shifts. The Barrow Collapse timer advances by 1.' 'That's a Miss — you're pinned by a rock. Mark 1 Harm and the timer advances by 1.'
tutorialTactics.track_timers_visibly: Keep the timers visible to players. Say: 'The Barrow Collapse timer is now at 2 out of 6. The barrow is groaning — you can feel the stones shifting.' This makes the pressure tangible.
tutorialTactics.encourage_creativity: When a player describes a creative action, reward it. Say: 'That's a clever idea — I'll lower the DV to 2 because of your approach.' This teaches that creativity matters.
tutorialTactics.use_story_beats: When a player fails a roll, say: 'That's a Miss. You gain a Story Beat, and I'm going to spend one to make things interesting...' Then introduce a complication. This teaches the SB economy.
tutorialTactics.summarize_lessons: At the end of each scene, briefly summarize: 'So in this scene, you learned how Position works, how to use Boons, and how Timers build tension. In the next scene, we'll look at social encounters and alternative resolutions.' This reinforces learning.
